sentences.text: In the early 1970s, hospitals accepted responsibility for ensuring that recurrent expenditure was less than their approved budget, but it was largely left to others to finance capital expenditure that hospitals expected to make over the longer term.

At the end of the 1970s, the federal share of provincial hospital and physician expenditures reached a high of almost 60%, but by the end of the 1990s this had declined to a low of slightly more than 41%.
Federal cash-only transfers for hospital and physician expenditures ranged from a high of close to 47% in 1976/77 to a low of 14.6% in 1998/99.
